title: Tech Note: Optimizing Record Selections - Part 1 — Under the Hood of the 4D Data File

historical_commentary.text: This note explains the internal organization of the classic 4D binary data file on disk and in memory as background for optimizing record selections in large, multi-user deployments; the specific binary .4DB/.4DC data file architecture it describes has been long superseded by 4D's modern structure file format, though the general goal of understanding storage internals to optimize performance at scale remains a relevant engineering principle.
related_updates: The classic binary 4D data file architecture described here (as it existed across 4D v3 and v6) has been superseded by 4D's modern structure file format
Modern 4D includes substantially different storage, indexing, and caching mechanisms than the v3/v6-era data file internals discussed in this note
